## Purpose

This SOP details the procedures for safely operating the EA Program's
DJI unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs/drones) for research image
collection [@dji_mavic3pro; @dji_matrice100]. It covers pre-flight
setup, flight operations, image collection, post-flight procedures,
and data transfer. Images obtained from these aircraft are used for
photogrammetry (3D modeling), site monitoring, vegetation mapping,
and other remote sensing applications.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All flights of EA Program drones, including the DJI
  Mavic 3 Pro and DJI Matrice 100, for research and instructional
  purposes
- **Does not apply to:** Indoor flights; flights conducted by
  contracted third-party operators; processing of drone imagery beyond
  data transfer (see future SOP-L805)
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites and approved flying areas


## Definitions

- **AGL (Above Ground Level):** Flight altitude measured from the
  ground surface directly below the aircraft, not from mean sea level;
  FAA Part 107 limits sUAS to 400 feet AGL (approximately 122 m) in
  uncontrolled airspace [@faa_part107].
- **Compass calibration:** A pre-flight procedure that orients the
  drone's internal compass to the local magnetic field; required at
  each new site or after transporting the aircraft; performed by
  rotating the aircraft in specific orientations per the DJI app
  prompts [@dji_mavic3pro].
- **DJI Mavic 3 Pro:** A compact foldable quadcopter with a
  three-camera Hasselblad system; the EA Program's primary survey
  aircraft stored in SGM 106; flight time approximately 43 minutes;
  maximum wind resistance 12 m/s (Beaufort 6) [@dji_mavic3pro].
- **DJI Matrice 100:** A legacy quadcopter platform capable of
  carrying a research payload of up to 1 kg; stored in SGM 210;
  suited for multi-sensor work; requires the DJI Pilot app for
  operation [@dji_matrice100].
- **Gimbal:** The motorized, stabilized mount that holds the camera;
  compensates for drone movement to produce level, stable imagery;
  always reinstall the gimbal guard during transport.
- **LAANC (Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability):**
  An FAA system that provides near-real-time airspace authorization
  for UAS operations in controlled airspace (Classes B, C, D, and E
  surface areas); authorization is obtained through the B4UFLY or
  Aloft apps before each flight in controlled airspace
  [@faa_b4ufly; @faa_part107].
- **LiPo battery (lithium polymer battery):** The rechargeable battery
  used in DJI drones; stores significant energy and poses a fire
  hazard if punctured, short-circuited, or charged incorrectly; must
  be stored at 40--60% charge for long-term storage and kept away from
  flammable materials.
- **Nadir angle:** A camera gimbal angle of -90°, pointing the camera
  directly downward toward the ground surface; the standard angle for
  photogrammetric mapping and orthomosaic generation.
- **Part 107:** Title 14 CFR Part 107 of the Code of Federal
  Regulations, governing Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems; requires a
  Remote Pilot Certificate for commercial and research operations;
  specifies operating limitations including maximum altitude, VLOS
  requirement, and prohibited airspace [@faa_part107].
- **Photogrammetry:** The science of making measurements from
  photographs; in the drone context, software such as Reality Capture
  or Pix4D processes overlapping aerial images to produce 3D models,
  dense point clouds, digital surface models (DSMs), and georeferenced
  orthomosaics [@realitycapture_docs].
- **RTH (Return to Home):** An automated failsafe function that
  returns the drone to its recorded home point (takeoff location) if
  the controller signal is lost or the battery reaches the RTH
  threshold; the home point must be set before each flight.
- **sUAS (small Unmanned Aircraft System):** FAA classification for
  unmanned aircraft weighing less than 55 pounds (25 kg); both EA
  Program drones qualify as sUAS [@faa_part107].
- **TRUST (The Recreational UAS Safety Test):** An FAA-mandated online
  safety test for recreational flyers; required when operating under
  the Exception for Limited Recreational Operations (44809) rather
  than Part 107.
- **UAS (Unmanned Aircraft System):** The complete system including
  the drone, remote controller, and associated software.
- **VLOS (Visual Line of Sight):** FAA requirement that the Remote
  Pilot maintain unaided visual contact with the aircraft at all times
  during flight; flight beyond VLOS requires a Part 107 waiver
  [@faa_part107].


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                   |
|:------------------|:-------------------------------------------------|
| PI                | Approve flight plans; ensure FAA compliance      |
| Certified Pilot   | Hold FAA Part 107 certificate; conduct flights   |
| Visual Observer   | Maintain visual contact with the drone; alert
                      pilot to hazards                                    |
| New Students      | Complete training before any drone operation     |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-danger}
### Critical Safety Rules

- Never fly over people who are not directly participating in the
  operation
- Never fly beyond visual line of sight (VLOS)
- Never fly near other aircraft or in restricted airspace without
  authorization
- Never touch spinning propellers
- Never fly under the influence of alcohol or drugs
:::

### Hazards

- **Physical:** Spinning propellers can cause lacerations. A drone
  falling from altitude can cause blunt force injury. LiPo batteries
  may be hot after flight.
- **Regulatory:** Unauthorized flights can result in FAA fines and
  criminal penalties [@faa_part107].
- **Property:** Crashes can damage the drone (replacement cost several
  thousand dollars) and property below.
- **Environmental:** Drones can disturb nesting birds and wildlife.
  Avoid flying near known nesting sites during breeding season.

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses (recommended during takeoff and landing)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)
- [ ] Closed-toe shoes

### Emergency Procedures

If the drone loses connection, activate RTH immediately. If RTH fails,
allow the drone to execute its failsafe. Do not attempt to catch a
falling drone. Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd).


## FAA Regulations

::: {.callout-important}
### Legal Requirement
All drone flights must comply with current FAA regulations. The pilot
is personally responsible for compliance [@faa_part107].
:::

Research operations require FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot certification.
Flights in controlled airspace (near airports) require prior LAANC
authorization via the B4UFLY or Aloft apps [@faa_b4ufly]. Pomona
College campus is within Ontario International Airport (KONT) Class C
airspace; LAANC authorization is required for on-campus flights.
Both EA Program drones are registered with the FAA; registration
numbers are on file with the PI and must be displayed on the aircraft
at all times.

### Flight Restrictions under Part 107

- Maximum altitude: 400 feet AGL [@faa_part107]
- Daylight operations only (civil twilight with anti-collision
  lighting permissible with appropriate equipment)
- Visual line of sight at all times
- No flights over non-participating persons
- Yield right of way to manned aircraft at all times

### Software

| Application            | Purpose                                    |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| DJI Fly or DJI Pilot   | Flight control, camera settings, flight planning [@dji_mavic3pro; @dji_matrice100] |

## Procedure

### Pre-Flight Inspection

1. Inspect the airframe: no cracks, loose propellers, or debris in
   motors.
2. Charge all batteries to 100% before departure.
3. Check the DJI app for firmware updates; update if prompted
   [@dji_mavic3pro].

### Pre-Flight Checks at the Site

1. Perform compass calibration per the DJI app [@dji_mavic3pro].
2. Check airspace: open B4UFLY or Aloft and verify authorization
   [@faa_b4ufly].
3. Record weather conditions in the flight log.

### Flight Operations

1. Announce "Taking off" to all personnel.
2. Hover at 3--5 m to verify stable flight, GPS lock, and camera
   orientation.
3. Execute the flight plan:
   - For photogrammetry: use automated waypoint or grid mode with
     70--80% front overlap and 60--70% side overlap [@realitycapture_docs].
   - For manual survey: fly in a systematic pattern at the planned
     altitude.
4. Monitor battery: begin return at 30%; land immediately at 20%.
5. Announce "Landing" before descent.

### Image Collection Settings

| Setting               | Recommended Value                    |
|:----------------------|:-------------------------------------|
| Image format          | JPEG + RAW (DNG) for photogrammetry  |
| Photo interval        | 2 seconds (timed shot for grid plans)|
| Resolution            | Maximum available                     |
| Gimbal angle          | Nadir (-90°) for mapping; oblique (-45°) for 3D models |

### Post-Flight Procedures

1. Power off the drone and remote controller.
2. Replace the gimbal cover.
3. Remove the MicroSD card and transfer images:
   - Create a folder: `Drone_SiteID_YYYYMMDD_AltitudeAGL`
   - Copy all images; verify file count
4. Format the MicroSD card after confirming backup.
5. Return all equipment to storage (Mavic to SGM 106; Matrice to
   SGM 210).
6. Complete the flight log: aircraft, date, location, pilot, duration,
   battery cycles used, any incidents.


## Quality Control

- Complete the pre-flight checklist before every flight.
- Verify GPS lock (minimum 8 satellites) before takeoff.
- After each flight, review a sample of images to confirm coverage,
  focus, and exposure.
- Report any incidents (crashes, near-misses, property damage) to the
  PI within 24 hours. FAA reporting may be required for incidents
  involving injury or property damage exceeding $500 [@faa_part107].

## Training Record

Before operating any EA Program drone independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) in full
2. Hold a current FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot certificate, or have
   passed TRUST (for recreational operations under direct PI
   supervision) [@faa_part107]
3. Complete the DJI app tutorial and demonstrate proficiency with
   simulator mode [@dji_mavic3pro]
4. Demonstrate pre-flight inspection, calibration, takeoff, hover,
   controlled flight pattern, and landing under supervision
5. Complete at least one supervised photogrammetry data collection
   flight with acceptable image quality
6. Be signed off by the PI
